lines.text: Hi! This is a MyCast demo. Today we are in Pompeii, near Naples.
The city that stopped in AD 79. What happened?
Mount Vesuvius erupted. Pompeii, along with Herculaneum and Stabiae, was buried under four to six metres of volcanic ash and pumice.
Estimates range from ten to twenty thousand. It was a wealthy town with fine public buildings and luxurious houses.
Do we know how it all unfolded?
We have an eyewitness: the letters of Pliny the Younger, who watched the eruption from across the bay. The exact day is still debated: traditionally August, but newer finds point to autumn.
Why is Pompeii so important to science?
Because the ash preserved the city almost whole. UNESCO calls it the only site that gives a complete picture of an ancient Roman city.
And there is graffiti too, right?
Hundreds of wall inscriptions. Scholars use them to study everyday spoken Latin, not the Latin of the classical writers.
What about those famous figures of people?
The bodies decayed and left hollows in the ash. Archaeologists filled them with plaster and got casts of people's last moments.
Haunting and moving at once. Today millions of visitors come every year.
That was a MyCast demo episode. You can build your own podcast at mycast.pro.
